I checked all 6 foregrounds against both backgrounds at 4.5 with OKCA (`klar contrast`). Of the 12 pairs, 7 fail, and 2 more are same-color pairs that can't occur. Nothing has been edited in the file.

## Results

| Foreground | on `surface` #fff | on `surface-dark` #1a1a2e |

| text #1a1a2e | 15.8 ✅ | n/a, same color as the background |

`text` is meant for light surfaces and `inverse` for dark ones, so those two combinations don't apply.

## Proposed fixes

A single value can't pass on both backgrounds, so each failing token needs a per-surface variant. I fixed the background and moved the foreground. Lightness moves first. Chroma is reduced only where lightness alone can't reach 4.5.

| Token | Background | Current → proposed | Contrast | Change (ΔE) | What moves |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| primary | surface | #3b82f6 → **#115bcc** | 5.0 | 15 | lightness only (L 0.62→0.50) |
| accent | surface | #e94560 → **#bf103f** | 4.7 | 13 | lightness only (L 0.63→0.52) |
| success | surface | #22c55e → **#047f38** | 4.6 | 22 | lightness and chroma (L 0.72→0.52, C 0.19→0.14) |
| muted | surface-dark | #666666 → **#919191** | 4.7 | 17 | lightness only |
| success | surface-dark | #22c55e → **#41d870** | 4.8 | 5 | lightness only (L 0.72→0.78) |
| primary | surface-dark | #3b82f6 → **#7bacfc** | 4.5 | 13 | lightness and chroma (C 0.19→0.13) |
| accent | surface-dark | #e94560 → **#fe8a93** | 4.6 | 14 | lightness and chroma (C 0.20→0.14) |

## Things to decide

- **Desaturation is a design call.** Three fixes (success on light, primary on dark, accent on dark) can't reach 4.5 by lightness alone, because the colors hit the sRGB gamut ceiling. I used `--allow-desaturation` for those, and they're the paler or duller results. If the brand saturation matters more, the alternative is to keep those colors for large text or UI components only (3:1 threshold) and not use them as body text.
- **Largest changes:** success on light (ΔE 22) and muted on dark (ΔE 17). The smallest is success on dark (ΔE 5).
- **Contrast values are rounded.** Two fixes (primary on dark, 4.5, and success on light, 4.6) sit right at the threshold, so add a little margin if you'd rather not sit on the line.

I can write these into `tokens-system.json` as `-on-light` and `-on-dark` variants if you'd like.

**Dark-mode primary: `#7bacfc`**. It scores OKCA 4.5 as foreground on `#1a1a2e`, which is the AA body-text minimum. It is the closest passing color, but it is a noticeable drift from the brand blue, so it needs a brand sign-off.

- **The brand blue fails as-is.** `#3b82f6` on `#1a1a2e` scores OKCA 1.9.
- **Lightness alone can't fix it.** `klar find` can only lighten, and it tops out at `#438aff` with OKCA 2.2, still failing. At this saturation the blue has no lighter version that displays in sRGB.
- **Chroma has to give.** Reducing chroma from 0.188 to 0.128 and raising lightness from 0.648 to 0.743 reaches 4.5. Hue is preserved (259.8° → 259.85°).
- **Drift is deltaE 13 from `#3b82f6`.** That is "clearly different" on the scale (11+), though well short of the 20+ that would read as a different color. It reads as a lighter, softer blue of the same family.

The 4.5 is exact with no headroom. If you want a margin against rounding or renderer differences, a slightly lighter blue costs a little more drift. I can produce that if you'd like.

If that shift is too much for the brand, the alternative is to keep `#3b82f6` in dark mode for large text and UI elements only (threshold 3.0) and use `#7bacfc` for body text. I checked every foreground against both backgrounds with OKCA, foreground on background, at the 4.5 body-text threshold. 7 of the 10 distinct pairs fail. The other 3 pass: `text` and `muted` on `surface`, and `inverse` on `surface-dark`. `text` on `surface-dark` and `inverse` on `surface` are the same color pairs, so I skipped them. No token is outside sRGB.

## Failing pairs and fixes

| Foreground | Background | OKCA now | Proposed fix | OKCA after | Color change (deltaE) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| accent `#e94560` | surface `#fff` | 2.8 | `#bf103f` | 4.7 | 13 (clearly different) |
| primary `#3b82f6` | surface `#fff` | 2.9 | `#115bcc` | 5.0 | 15 (clearly different) |
| success `#22c55e` | surface `#fff` | 1.9 | `#047f38` | 4.6 | 22 (very different) |
| muted `#666` | surface-dark `#1a1a2e` | 2.4 | `#919191` | 4.7 | 17 (clearly different) |
| success `#22c55e` | surface-dark `#1a1a2e` | 3.4 | `#41d870` | 4.8 | 5 (noticeable, subtle) |
| accent `#e94560` | surface-dark `#1a1a2e` | 2.0 | `#fe8a93` | 4.6 | 14 (clearly different) |
| primary `#3b82f6` | surface-dark `#1a1a2e` | 1.9 | `#7bacfc` | 4.5 | 13 (clearly different) |

Changing lightness alone fixes the first five rows, and the hue is unchanged. For the last two rows, and for `success` on `surface` (the third row), lightness alone can't reach 4.5. The best lightness-only result tops out at 2.2 for `success` on white and `primary` on dark. For `accent` on dark it tops out at 2.8. Those three fixes also reduce saturation.

## Decisions for you

- **Success on white (`#047f38`, deltaE 22):** this is the biggest change in the audit. The green goes from bright to a deep forest green.
- **Accent and primary on dark:** these fixes are lighter and less saturated (`#fe8a93`, `#7bacfc`), which reads as pastel next to the brand colors.
- **Not applied:** I have only quoted these as proposals. The saturation cost is a brand call.
- **One token, two values:** `primary`, `accent` and `success` each need a different value per background. That means separate light-theme and dark-theme tokens. One value can't pass on both, because a light-on-dark fix fails on white and the reverse.
- **Cheaper fix:** if `primary`, `accent` or `success` is only used for large text (24px or more) or for UI components, the threshold is 3.0. On dark, `success` already passes at 3.4. The other failing pairs would still need smaller nudges.

If you want a more vivid green or amber, the choice is between accepting lower saturation and using those hues only at large-text size (3.0).
